BST260 Final Project Proposal

To BST260 Teaching Team, Fall 2026

William Bonaventura

2027-06-09

Source: vignettes/proposal.qmd

Analysis 1:

Research Question:

Among those outbreaks where drinking water was responsible, how is water type related to the presence of >= 1 death stemming from the outbreak, adjusting for etiology and illnesses.

Unit of Analysis and Population

The unit of analysis is a specific waterborne illness outbreak. The original dataset was provided by the CDC, and for the purposes of this analysis, the population at hand is all waterborne outbreaks in which the type of exposure included drinking water. The sample size for this population is 1286 (pre-removal of missing data, other decisions, etc.).

Exposure Variable(s)

The exposure variable(s) in this analysis include our main effect ‘water type’, as well as covariates (and potential confounders) etiology and number of illnesses. Water type I will code as (nominal) categorical, and will exclude units of analysis with missing information (or of unknown type). Etiology will also be coded categorically, while illnesses will be coded as (numeric) continuous. As for the main effect, those outbreaks with either missing etiological or illness data will be excluded.

Outcome Variable

The outcome variable in this analysis will be coded into a binary (dichotomous) outcome variable representing whether or not >= 1 death occured from this outbreak. Therefore, it is dichotomous categorical, and will be assessed via a logistic regression model.

Confounder(s)

The potential confounders I choose to assess for this analysis include etiology and illnesses. Regarding etiology, I choose this as different pathogens vary in their lethality, and this etiology may also be assocatied with the particular water type. It will be coded a nominal categorical variables. Regarding illnesses, this serves as a proxy covariate representing the spread (person-count wise) of the outbreak, which influences the presence of >=1 deaths of the outbreak, and may be assocaited with water type.

Analysis 2:

Research Question:

Has the age-adjusted firearm mortality rate changed differently, from 2005 to 2024, across different US census regions? Put another way, is census region an effect modifier in the relationship between time and age-adjusted fire arm mortality rate.

Unit of Analysis and Population

The unit of analysis here is the specific firearm mortality information for a particular state, for a particular year. The population is state firearm mortality data between the years of 2005 and 2024, and is provided in a dataset from the CDC.

Exposure Variable(s)

Our main effect exposure variable will be continuous year, and will ran from 2005 to 2024. I will code it as a numeric, continuous variable. Our other covariate, for which we are assessing as a potential effect modifier, will be a new variable (that I will defined and code) called region. This will be coded at a (nominal) categorical variable, and will have several categories.

Outcome Variable

The outcome variable here is a continuous variable that represents the age-adjusted firearm mortality rate (per 100,000 people)

Confounder(s)

Due to how few variables are included in this CDC dataset, I am not considering potential confounder covariates in this analysis.
